ruling.recommended_action: Refund $1.13 (voucher, per NS-7) to the rider for the unexempt 0.80 km off-route segment; record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file; no account flag (RD-6 conditions unmet).

segment_findings.reason: The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped (F9); the only rider message before the 22:57 segment is a pickup-location note at 22:45 (F7) and the only driver message is an arrival note at 22:46 naming no road or route (F8), so no rider agreement to any named route precedes the segment; the driver's later statement (F10) is not rider consent [RD-5]. No stop is measured in this segment and no rider-named place exists (F7, F8) [RD-3]. RD-4(a) is failed by the absence of any incident (F14) and the band facts (F11, F12) cannot exempt alone [RD-4]. The 0.80 km extra_km therefore counts under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Partly rejected as to quantum: it implies the whole 12.4 km / $2.33 excess is recoverable, but under RD-2 only the measured unexempt segment's extra_km counts — the other 0.80 km of the 1.6 km total (F1, F3, F4) is not attributable to any off-route segment and is not refundable [F1][F3][F4][RD-2].

Rejected: flag_account under RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in the 90-day window; F17 shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so this case is not 'repeated' within that window, and the trace marks RD-6 unmet [F17][RD-6].
Accepted only in part; it does not defeat liability, since the 0.80 km segment (F3) is itself an unexempt deviation under RD-1/RD-2 and the complaint is upheld to that extent [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

Rejected: the Ayer Rajah Expressway band-1 record (F11) is a speed band, not an RD-4(a) traffic incident, and RD-4(b) corroboration cannot exempt a segment on its own; no incident was recorded near the route (F14) [F11][F14][RD-4].

Rejected as an exemption: congestion elsewhere on the corridor (F12, F13) and light rain (F15) are not tied to the replaced stretch of the optimal route and are not RD-4(a) incidents (F14) [F12][F13][F14][F15][RD-4].

Rejected: a time window matching the trip is not route evidence, and no fact links F11/F12 to the replaced portion of the optimal route; the exemption burden under RD-4 lies on the driver who rerouted [F11][F12][F3][RD-4].
Rejected: RD-4(b) states a band alone does not exempt in this MVP; F14 (no incidents) is fatal to RD-4(a) [F14][F11][F12][RD-4].

Rejected: RD-1's 'reasonable cause' qualification must be evidenced as RD-4 prescribes, and the only evidence is congestion bands with no incident and no link to the replaced stretch (F11, F12, F14) [F3][F11][F12][F14][RD-1][RD-4].
Rejected as irrelevant: no stop or add-on is alleged; F6 shows waiting $0.00 and no destination-change fee, so RD-3 does not apply on these facts [F6][F3][RD-3].

Rejected: the complete timestamped log (F9) shows only two arrival messages, both before the 22:57 deviation (F3), which proves the absence of consent rather than a normal traffic-driven choice; the driver's post-trip statement (F10) is not evidence of prior agreement [F7][F8][F9][F10][F3][RD-5].

Rejected in part: no account flag is imposed because RD-6's conditions are unmet (F17), which is what the driver asked for; but his profile does not make the unexempt 0.80 km deviation lawful under RD-1/RD-2 [F3][F17][RD-1][RD-2][RD-6].
